newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa falls amid renewed origin, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa falls amid renewed origin, fund selling.

text.p: Cocoa futures fell amid renewed origin and fund selling, traders said.
Sterling's strength against other European currencies also had a bearish impact, they said.
But resistance on May at 847 sterling remained intact.
Before the midday break, May last traded at 860 stg, 8 lower, having seen a low of 857 stg. Volume on May was 1,822 lots.
The most active contract was July, which last traded down 7 stg at 881 stg on volume of 1,952 lots.
Total volume for the morning was 6,759 lots.
The technical outlook remained poor and despite opening calls which suggested a rise, traders said they had been expecting cocoa to go lower.
"It's no surprise to the market to see cocoa coming down," one said.
There were origin sellers applying clear fundamental pressure to the market.
"It's the same old story," another trader said. "A strong sterling means more Ivory Coast hedging and less industry buying." There was also selling by funds, he said.

The technical picture was bearish, he said, while talk that Ivory Coast arrivals might be better than expected contributed to the bearish outlook. Reports that favourable weather might help the crop also weighed on cocoa.

One analyst saw an assault on the psychological 850 stg level basis May, while the previous second month low of 847 stg, hit on July 31, 1995 is also seen as a possible target and is cited by analysts as the current support point for cocoa.
